native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA on the 12 forms of capital analyzed in 100-year time slices, PC1 (≈30% of variance) is an aggregate capital-accumulation axis. Both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) are characterized by strongly negative PC1 scores — i.e. low capital accumulation relative to the full series. The Middle Neolithic is a declining segment, falling from PC1 ≈ −0.58 (3400 BCE) to ≈ −1.78 (3000 BCE, the series low; mean ≈ −1.37). The Younger Neolithic remains low and broadly stable (mean ≈ −1.12, range −0.41 to −1.60, a slight recovery by 2300 BCE). All 12 phase bins fall below the 0.0 full-series mean (ranks 6–22 of 39). Secondary pollen context (Belau openness) declines through the Middle Neolithic and stays low through the Younger Neolithic, consistent with a low-accumulation, less-open landscape.
native_result.WorkflowB: Load capital.csv; drop group & color; convert comma-decimal strings to float on the 12 Z-columns; re-standardize (mean 0, unit variance); run PCA via SVD on the 39×12 matrix; extract PC1 scores per 100-yr bin; characterize MN (3400–3000) and SG/YN (2900–2300) by mean level, within-window trend, and rank/position vs the full series; cross-check with Belau pollen SMOOTH_MEAN_100y aligned via calBP=BCE+1950.
